t: You're standing in Mitre Square, a small square in Aldgate, inside the City of London. It measures roughly twenty-three metres by twenty-four, and three passages connect it to Mitre Street, Creechurch Place and, by St James's Passage, Duke's Place. It is known as the place where Catherine Eddowes died in 1888. She was the fourth of the five canonical victims of the unidentified serial killer known as Jack the Ripper, who attacked women in Whitechapel and Spitalfields that autumn.
